result.impl:
Four of the five masters are rebuilt in place and verified in close-ups and in the town. Hydrangea didn't need a rebuild because its fix was in the leaf texture. Nothing called `make_willow`, `make_birch`, `make_pine` or `make_bush` in any Blender text, so I found each master's parameters by matching seeds. Each one reproduced the old mesh exactly (positions, vertex colours, normals, materials). I rebuilt with those parameters and the default `nk_finish` arguments:

| Master | Call |
|---|---|
| Willow | `make_willow(k,51)` |
| Birch | `make_birch(k,41)` |
| Birch_Single | `make_birch(k,43,H=7.5,stems=1)` |
| Pine_A | `make_pine(k,21,H=10.0)` |
| Pine_B | `make_pine(k,27,H=13.0,Rmax_f=0.26)` |
| Pine_Young | `make_pine(k,29,H=5.0,young=True)` |
| Hydrangea (not rebuilt) | `make_bush(k,107,[("hydrangea",0.75),("broadleaf_dark",0.25)],R=1.0,H=1.2,nclump=4,cards=22)` |

**What changed, in `vk_nature.py` (pushed to the Blender text):**
- **Shared change:** new `cut_branch(b,frac)`. `bark_tubes` takes three new optional settings per branch depth: `cut` (where the tube stops), `rscale` (thinner), `ao` (darker). The leaf cards don't move. Other callers are unaffected.
- **Willow:** same trunk, limbs and random draws. The 150 hair cards and 90-card curtain are replaced by 14 drooping leaf clumps of 21 "willow" cards each, laid over each clump and hanging past its lower edge. On top of that is a lighter curtain of about 35 strands at the rim (from 44 slots with 20% skipped).
  - Normals are spherical, with the downward part flattened below the middle of the canopy.
  - The darkness floor under the canopy is 0.72, so the underside renders mid-green, not black.
  - Limb tubes stop at 82% and are slightly darker, so they no longer poke out of the top.
  - Size: 8.63 × 8.56 × 5.45 m (5.0 m above ground), 95% of the leaves within 3.98 m of the trunk. Vertices went from 2360 to 4288.
- **Birch and Birch_Single:** white bark stays on the stems. Branches now use the oak bark, are 0.85× as thick, stop at 80% of their length and are darker (0.6). The canopy is unchanged.
- **Pine A, B and Young:** whorl branches are 0.6× as thick, stop at 65% of their length and are much darker (0.42). The trunk inside the crown is darkened down to 0.5. The needle cards are unchanged.

**Hydrangea (`vk_leafgen.py`):** the three flower heads now have their own colours: lilac-blue, soft pink/white and soft blue. The blues are the old ones with about 35% less saturation; average flower saturation dropped from 0.48 to 0.29. The random draws are unchanged. A new `repaint_leaf_cell(cell)` repaints only the hydrangea square of the atlas. I first checked it rebuilds the old square exactly, and every pixel outside that square is identical to before. The height map is untouched.
- This overwrites the leaf texture file on disk, `VillageKit\Textures\T_VK_Leaves_BCA.png`, which is also re-packed in Blender. The original is backed up as `T_VK_Leaves_BCA_orig.png` in my scratchpad folder.

**Renders** are in `...\scratch-2026-09-23-d49817\renders2\nature\`:
- Before: `before_lineup`, `before_willow`, `before_willow_low`, `before_birch`, `before_pines`, `before_hydrangea`, `before_colony` (.png)
- After, test area: `after_willow`, `after_willow_low`, `after_willow_colony`, `after_birch`, `after_birch_close`, `after_pines`, `after_hydrangea`, `after_colony`
- After, real instances: `after_town_willow_colony`, `after_town_willow_close` (Willow_inst.002 at 1662.5, 30.9), `after_town_ridge_colony`, `after_town_ridge_side`, `after_town_hydrangea`
- The `wip_*` files are intermediate tries.

The temporary collection and objects are deleted and the .blend was not saved.

**Still open:**
- The willow still uses the thin-strand "willow" texture square, so its outline stays a little wispy from the top-down camera. The dome is now lumpy clumps rather than combed hair.
- Some orange pine bark still shows through gaps in the crown. It's darker but not hidden.
- VK_ValleyTown now has only three willows, at x ≈ 1504, 1662 and 1715; none are left at (1530–1560, 30–55). Another agent probably re-placed them, so I rendered the one at 1662.5.
- The master user counts also dropped between my first check and the rebuild (willow 22 to 8, Pine_A 423 to 297). The rebuild itself changed no counts.

problems: [MEDIUM] Willow from the colony camera (40 m, 50 deg pitch) still reads as a fine-hatched, stringy olive mop. The 14 new clumps can't be read at gameplay distance because the thin-strand 'willow' atlas cell turns every clump into vertical striations. There are none of the chunky lumps the oak and birch show in the same frame. The willow is also duller: measured foliage saturation 0.73 vs 0.86-0.88 for birch and oak. See crit_colony_willow.png, crit_colony_row1_willow_vs_oak.png and crit_town_willow1504_colony.png. The 'dark' half of the complaint is fixed. Mean luminance is willow 0.20 vs oak 0.17 (top half 0.18 vs oak top 0.16), so it is no longer a dark outlier. It is still 'hairy'.

[MEDIUM] Willow's far/top half is in shade from the colony camera (crit_colony_willow.png, crit_willow_top.png, crit_colony_willow_fromN.png). Likely cause is wfns.nfn in vk_nature.py, which uses q=(d.x/R,d.y/R,d.z/Rz) normalised. That treats the flat 3.9 x 2.3 m dome as a sphere, not as an ellipsoid (the true gradient would be d/R^2). The top clumps' normals point too far sideways, so with the 37 deg sun the north half of the crown sits near the shadow line. Suggested fix: use ellipsoid-gradient normals or add more UP bias on the crown clumps.

[LOW] Willow's upper outline at eye level is bristly: strand and card tips flick upward along the whole top edge (crit_eye_willow_S.png, crit_eye_willow_N.png). This works against the weeping read. Straight top-down, ground shows through 5-6 gaps between crown clumps (crit_willow_top.png); the gaps don't show at 50 deg.

[LOW] Pines A, B and Young: the trunk leader (BARK_PINE) runs almost to the needle top (Pine_A 9.71 vs 10.02 m, Pine_B 12.71 vs 13.12 m, Young 4.71 vs 4.86 m). The six apex cards splay outward, so the leader shows from above as a red/orange dash at the tip of every crown. On the north-ridge forest this becomes a repeated red-speck pattern (crit_town_ridge_colony.png, crit_town_ridge_colony_zoom.png, crit_colony_zoom_pineA/B/Y.png).

[LOW] Pine_Young: the top whorl's branch tubes are still visible from above as a dark-red six-spoke star around the apex (crit_close_pineY_top.png). Each branch's two rolled needle cards form a V that opens upward, which exposes the axis to a high camera. At eye level, brown stubs still show between the lower whorls (crit_close_pineY_base.png). Much better than before, but not gone.

[LOW] Pine_B at eye level on the sun side: the orange trunk still reads as a bright vertical stripe through the lower ~60% of the crown (crit_eye_pines_S.png). The in-crown darkening only takes effect higher up.

[LOW] Birch and Birch_Single: the white twig slashes are gone from every angle checked (crit_colony_zoom_birch.png, crit_eye_birches_S/N.png). Remaining: the white stems (BARK_BIRCH up to 7.82 m of a 9.24 m tree) show through canopy gaps as short white dashes from some angles, most clearly from the west (crit_colony_zoom_birch_fromW.png, crit_eye_birch_W_close.png). The new dark branches read as thin near-black 'wires' below the canopy on the shade side (crit_eye_birches_N.png), and a few dark lines lie on the canopy top at zoom.

[INFO] Hydrangea resolved. The atlas diff against the backup T_VK_Leaves_BCA_orig.png is confined to x 1590-2000, y 599-983 (the hydrangea cell), alpha is unchanged, and only SM_VK_Bush_Hydrangea samples that cell. Mean saturation of the cell's opaque pixels (flowers and leaves together) dropped from 0.49 to 0.34 (-31%). Close up it is a lilac, soft-blue and salmon-pink mix with no vivid blue (crit_eye_hydrangea_S.png). From the colony camera in town the heads read as dark indigo/violet, about the same value as the lavender plots next to them. The pink heads aren't readable at 40 m and no white heads are visible (crit_town_hydrangea_colony.png). The bush is still ~2.8 m tall; the original review asked for 1.5-2 m, but that was outside this fix.

[INFO] No new technical artifacts found. No NaN or zero normals, degenerate faces or loose verts, all material slots valid, leaf UVs stay inside their atlas cells, and none of the rebuilt masters shows missing materials. Under the willow canopy is mid-green, not black (crit_eye_willow_under.png). Some leaf cards seen edge-on show as thin dark spikes at the birch and hydrangea edges; this is minor and existed before. Cleanup: VK_TmpNature, its objects, the TMPN ground mesh/material and the temporary comparison image are deleted. The masters are still hidden, their user counts are unchanged, and the .blend was not saved.
